knowledge:
- key_parameters: protein.data=Input data frame of protein abundance across fractions ;; id=Identifier type (default "UNIPROT") to convert to gene symbols in convert2symbol() ;; dims=t-SNE dimensionality (2 or 3) ;; theta=t-SNE speed/accuracy trade-off parameter ;; perplexity=t-SNE perplexity parameter ;; min.psm=Minimum peptide-spectrum-matching count for filtering relocated candidates ;; pearson.cor=Pearson correlation coefficient threshold for filtering relocated candidates
- alternatives: None mentioned.
- when_to_use: Use when analyzing mass-spectrometry based spatial proteomics data (specifically fractionation-based proteomics with replicates) to map protein subcellular localization, evaluate co-localization, detect differential localization between conditions, or perform peptide/exon/transcript-centric localization.
- pitfalls: Replicates must be named with ".A." and ".B." respectively ;; Input data must use gene symbols for protein identification; other identifiers must be converted using convert2symbol() which may cause minor ID loss ;; Low marker protein coverage (recommended at least 20% coverage per compartment; if lower, redo fractionation or increase MS analytical depth) ;; t-SNE can be misleading if not well optimized; grid search optimization is recommended ;; Reducing t-SNE dimensionality to 2D (dims = 2) results in loss of information and underestimation of data resolution compared to 3D (dims = 3) ;; Exon-centric classification enriches more noise than gene-centric classification due to analytical depth.

workflows.name: gene_centric_classification
workflows.intent: Classify protein subcellular localization at compartment and neighborhood levels using a gene-centric approach.
input: protein_abundance.tsv (data.frame of protein abundance across fractions with replicates .A. and .B.)
psm_counts.tsv (data.frame of PSM counts for barcode plotting)
workflows.stages: 1. Load and log2-transform protein data ;; 2. Convert identifiers to gene symbols if necessary ;; 3. Calculate covered marker proteins ;; 4. Perform quality control on marker proteins ;; 5. Optimize and visualize marker proteins in t-SNE space ;; 6. Train SVM classifier and predict probabilities ;; 7. Estimate and apply compartment-level thresholds ;; 8. Estimate and apply neighborhood-level thresholds ;; 9. Merge compartment and neighborhood classifications ;; 10. Plot single protein barcode or multiple proteins
workflows.code:
df <- loadData(protein.data = hcc827Ctrl)
#df <- convert2symbol(df = df, id = "UNIPROT")
set.seed(2)
df <- df[sample(nrow(df), 6000),]
c.prots <- calculateCoveredProtein(proteinIDs = rownames(df), 
                        markerproteins = markerProteins[,1]) 
r.markers <- markerQualityControl(coveredProteins = c.prots,protein.data = df)
set.seed(6)
tsne.map <- tsneVisualization(protein.data = df, 
                    markerProteins = r.markers, 
                    dims = 3, 
                    theta = c(0.1), 
                    perplexity = c(60)) 
set.seed(9)
tsne.map2 <- tsneVisualization(protein.data = df, 
                    markerProteins = r.markers, 
                    dims = 2, 
                    theta = c(0.5), 
                    perplexity = c(60))
set.seed(4)
cls <- svmClassification(markerProteins = r.markers, 
                                    protein.data = df, 
                                    markerprot.df = markerProteins)
test.A <- cls[[1]]$svm.test.prob.out
test.B <- cls[[2]]$svm.test.prob.out
all.A <- cls[[1]]$all.prot.pred
all.B <- cls[[2]]$all.prot.pred
t.c.df <- computeThresholdCompartment(test.repA = test.A, test.repB = test.B)
c.cls.df <- applyThresholdCompartment(all.repA = all.A, all.repB = all.B,
                                    threshold.df = t.c.df)
t.n.df <- computeThresholdNeighborhood(test.repA = test.A, test.repB = test.B)
n.cls.df <- applyThresholdNeighborhood(all.repA = all.A, all.repB = all.B, 
                                    threshold.df = t.n.df)
cls.df <- mergeCls(compartmentCls = c.cls.df, neighborhoodCls = n.cls.df)
plotBarcode(sampleClassification = cls.df, protein = "NLRP4",
        s1PSM = hcc827CtrlPSMCount)
proteasome26s <- c("PSMA7", "PSMC3","PSMA4", "PSMB4", 
                    "PSMB6", "PSMB5", "PSMC2","PSMC4",
                    "PSMB3", "PSMA6","PSMC5","PSMC6")
plotMultipleProtein(sampleClassification = cls.df, proteinList = proteasome26s)

workflows.name: differential_localization
workflows.intent: Compare protein subcellular localization between two conditions (e.g., control vs treatment) and filter high-confidence relocated candidates.
workflows.stages: 1. Visualize localization shifts between conditions using a sankey plot ;; 2. Filter and identify strong relocated candidates using PSM counts and correlation analysis
workflows.code:
sankeyPlot(sampleCls1 = cls.df, sampleCls2 = hcc827GEFClass)
candidate.df <- candidateRelocatedProteins(sampleCls1 = cls.df, 
                                s1PSM = hcc827CtrlPSMCount, 
                                s1Quant = hcc827Ctrl,
                                sampleCls2 = hcc827GEFClass,
                                s2PSM = hcc827GefPSMCount,
                                s2Quant = hcc827GEF,
                                min.psm = 2,
                                pearson.cor = 0.8)
candidate2.df <- candidateRelocatedProteins(sampleCls1 = cls.df,
                                s1PSM = hcc827CtrlPSMCount, 
                                s1Quant = hcc827Ctrl, 
                                sampleCls2 = hcc827GEFClass, 
                                s2PSM = hcc827GefPSMCount, 
                                s2Quant = hcc827GEF, 
                                annotation = TRUE, 
                                min.psm = 9, 
                                pearson.cor = 0.05)

workflows.name: exon_centric_classification
workflows.intent: Classify subcellular localization at the exon/peptide level using a pre-built gene-centric model and compare results to detect deviated localizations.
input: gene_cls_model.rds (trained SVM model list from gene-centric workflow)
workflows.stages: 1. Extract trained models from the gene-centric classification ;; 2. Predict probabilities for exon-centric data ;; 3. Apply compartment thresholds ;; 4. Apply neighborhood thresholds ;; 5. Merge classifications ;; 6. Compare gene-centric and exon-centric classifications to detect deviations
workflows.code:
modelA <- cls[[1]]$model
modelB <- cls[[2]]$model
exon.cls <- svmExternalData(df = hcc827exon, modelA = modelA, modelB= modelB)
exon.A <- exon.cls[[1]]
exon.B <- exon.cls[[2]]
exon.comp.cls <- applyThresholdCompartment(all.repA = exon.A[,2:17], 
                                    all.repB = exon.B[,2:17],
                                    threshold.df = t.c.df)
exon.neigh.cls <- applyThresholdNeighborhood(all.repA = exon.A[,2:17], 
                                    all.repB = exon.B[,2:17], 
                                    threshold.df = t.n.df)
exon.cls.df <- mergeCls(compartmentCls = exon.comp.cls, 
                        neighborhoodCls = exon.neigh.cls)
exon.cls.df <- exon.cls.df[rownames(exon.A),]
exon.cls.df$GeneSymbol <- exon.A$Gene_Symbol
exon.cls.df$PeptideCount <- hcc827exon$PeptideCount
comp.df <- compareCls(geneCls = cls.df, exonCls = exon.cls.df)
